name: St. Moritz
tagline: Engadine glamour where alpine sport meets old-world luxury
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Sep, Oct, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: December to March for snow and the frozen-lake season of White Turf and Snow Polo; July and August for high-alpine hiking. Avoid the muddy shoulder weeks when much closes.

ourTake.lede: St. Moritz is at its best in winter, when the frozen lake becomes the whole point, this is where high-altitude sport meets old-money leisure, and you should lean into that rather than treat it as just a ski resort. Base yourself for the events and long lunches, not the piste-bashing; the skiing at neighbouring Corviglia and Corvatsch is good but the town's real currency is the après and the people-watching. Come in late January or February; a summer visit is quieter and lovelier for walking but misses the theatre.
ourTake.comeIf: You want the Alps at their most polished, long lunches on the piste, cashmere afternoons, and a grand old hotel where the staff remember your name.
ourTake.skipIf: You are chasing a lively nightlife scene or an affordable ski week; this is a small, formal, expensive village that sleeps early.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Badrutt's Palace Hotel
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: The turreted symbol of St. Moritz since 1896, the address the whole resort is measured against.

items.name: Kulm Hotel St. Moritz
items.description: Where Alpine winter tourism was invented in 1864, GaultMillau's Hotel of the Year, above the lake and the Cresta.

items.name: Suvretta House
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A fairytale castle on its own plateau, the only ski-in, ski-out house in St. Moritz, with a private lift to Corviglia.

items.name: Carlton Hotel St. Moritz
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A former tsar's residence turned all-suite house, every room faces the lake, and the finest Italian table in Switzerland is downstairs.

items.name: Kempinski Grand Hotel des Bains
items.description: A grand spa house on St. Moritz's mineral springs, the wellness address, at the foot of the Corviglia lift.

items.name: Grace La Margna St. Moritz
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A listed 1906 façade reborn as the resort's freshest luxury house, most rooms over the lake, two minutes from the station.

items.name: Grand Hotel Kronenhof
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A neo-Baroque grande dame facing the Bernina glaciers, the Engadin's most beautiful historic hotel, a short drive from St. Moritz.

items.name: Nira Alpina
credentials: Small Luxury Hotels of the World
items.description: A design-led mountain hotel with the Corvatsch cable car in the building, ski from bed to the glacier.

items.name: Corviglia & the Piz Nair Cable Car
items.description: The funicular climbs from the village directly to Corviglia at 2,489m, Switzerland's first railway built straight to a ski slope, opened in 1928, and a cable car floats the last 530m to the Piz Nair summit at 3,056m, where the whole Engadin lake plateau and the Albula Alps open below you. This is the home mountain of St. Moritz society, groomed to perfection and laced with sun terraces; ski it in winter or ride it up in summer for the view and lunch.

items.name: The Mountain-Restaurant Scene on Corviglia
items.description: Lunch on Corviglia is a St. Moritz institution, the long, champagne-fuelled midday table where the see-and-be-seen crowd gathers between runs. La Marmite at the top station is the legendary address for truffle and caviar, El Paradiso for its terrace and DJs, and Restaurant Piz Nair '10,000 Feet' the highest of them all. Book ahead; a private guide can arrange a table and a heli lift back.

items.name: Skiing Corviglia, 155km Above the Lakes
items.description: 155 kilometres of immaculately prepared pistes and 24 lifts spread across Corviglia's blues, reds and blacks, all facing the frozen chain of Engadin lakes, the birthplace of Alpine winter tourism still skiing at the top of the game. Private instructors and ski-in lunch reservations are the norm here, and the whole family can be matched to terrain, elders included.

items.name: Piz Nair Sunrise
items.description: On select winter mornings the Piz Nair cable car runs before dawn to carry a small group up to 3,056m for breakfast as the first light sets the Bernina peaks alight, followed by the first tracks down empty pistes. It is one of the Engadin's quietly magical private-feeling experiences, best arranged in advance with your hotel concierge.

items.name: Corvatsch, Cable Car to 3,303m
items.description: The Corvatsch is the highest point reachable by cable car in the whole of eastern Switzerland, rising from Surlej to a viewing platform at 3,303m that looks straight across the Bernina glaciers and down onto the string of turquoise Upper Engadin lakes. In winter it delivers long, high, snow-sure descents; in summer, glacier air and a terrace among the four-thousanders.

items.name: Corvatsch Snow Night & Hahnensee Run
items.description: Corvatsch runs Switzerland's longest floodlit night-skiing on Fridays, and its celebrated Hahnensee descent drops all the way from the glacier down to St. Moritz-Bad, a long, wild top-to-valley run that ends steps from an aprés-ski table. A memorable, slightly adventurous half-day for confident skiers in the family.

items.name: Diavolezza, The Glacier Panorama
items.description: The Diavolezza gondola lifts you to a terrace at 2,978m where Piz Bernina, the highest peak in the Eastern Alps at 4,049m, and the fluted ice of Piz Palü rise directly across the valley, with the Pers and Morteratsch glaciers spilling beneath your feet. The sun-terrace of the Berghaus here has one of the great glacier views in the Alps; go simply to look, or ski the powder.

items.name: The Morteratsch Glacier Hike & Glacier Trail
items.description: From Morteratsch station a gentle, well-marked trail follows the retreating tongue of the mighty Morteratsch glacier, with markers showing where the ice stood in past decades, a moving, easy walk suitable across generations. For the more adventurous, a guided glacier traverse descends from Diavolezza across the Pers and Morteratsch ice; take a certified mountain guide.

items.name: Muottas Muragl, The Funicular & the Sunset
items.description: A wonderfully old-fashioned funicular from 1907 climbs to a terrace at 2,454m that frames the classic Engadin postcard, the chain of lakes below, the Bernina massif beyond, painted gold at dusk. The funicular runs late into the evening precisely so you can stay for the alpenglow and dinner at the Romantik Hotel; the single best sunset in the valley.

items.name: The Muottas Muragl Philosophers' Path
items.description: From the mountain station a contemplative loop trail carries quotations from the great thinkers who summered in the Engadin, winding into the Val Muragl and back with the lakes always in view. It is a gentle, thoughtful walk, the Engadin's landscape has always drawn writers and philosophers, and this path makes that lineage tangible.

items.name: The Muottas Muragl Panorama Trail to Alp Languard
items.description: One of the Engadin's signature high-balcony walks traverses from Muottas Muragl toward Alp Languard, hung high above the valley the whole way with the lakes on one side and the Bernina glaciers on the other, through stone-pine forest. A chairlift down to Pontresina at the far end means you need only walk the beautiful part.

items.name: White Turf, Horse Racing on the Frozen Lake
items.description: Across three February Sundays the frozen lake becomes a racecourse and the definitive event of the St. Moritz winter season, thoroughbred flat and trotting races on snow, plus skijöring, the St. Moritz-exclusive discipline where skiers are hauled behind riderless horses at up to 50km/h. It is glamour, furs, champagne tents and society in full flourish; the hospitality marquees are the place to be.

items.name: The Snow Polo World Cup
items.description: Snow polo had its world premiere here in 1985, and St. Moritz still stages the only high-goal polo tournament played on snow, three days of thundering ponies on the frozen lake, VIP tents and end-of-day parties in late January. Among the most exclusive tickets of the European winter social calendar.

items.name: Cricket on Ice
items.description: First played on the frozen lake in 1988, Cricket on Ice is the delightfully improbable spectacle of a full match staged on the snow-covered surface of Lake St. Moritz in February, a natural draw for Indian visitors and a very St. Moritz blend of sport, eccentricity and lakeside hospitality.

items.name: The St. Moritz Gourmet Festival
items.description: Running since 1994, the region's landmark culinary festival brings guest chefs from around the world into the grand hotels for Four-Hands Dinners and the legendary Gourmet Safari that walks a small group through several palace kitchens in a single evening. The Engadin already carries eight Michelin stars; this is the week it shows off. (Note: repositioned to summer from 2026.)

items.name: The Segantini Museum
items.description: Built in 1908 as a memorial to the painter Giovanni Segantini, this domed stone rotunda holds the world's most important collection of his work, crowned by the monumental Alpine triptych 'La Vita, La Natura, La Morte'. Segantini reinvented how the high Alps were painted, and standing before the triptych with the real peaks outside is quietly extraordinary.

items.name: The Berry Museum
items.description: Set in the centuries-old Villa Arona in the heart of the village, this intimate house-museum shows the luminous, Belle Époque paintings of the physician-artist Peter Robert Berry, a warm, personal counterpoint to the grand hotels, and a window into the St. Moritz of a hundred years ago.

items.name: The Leaning Tower of St. Moritz
items.description: The last surviving fragment of the old church of St. Mauritius, this 12th-century tower leans at 5.5 degrees, a steeper tilt than Pisa's, above the village. A quick but characterful landmark, and a good anchor for a stroll through the old centre and up to Via Serlas.

items.name: Sils Maria & the Nietzsche House
items.description: The most serene of the Engadin villages sits between Lakes Sils and Silvaplana, and it was here, in a modest house from 1881 to 1888, that Friedrich Nietzsche spent seven summers and conceived much of his thought. The house is now a museum; the village itself, car-light, lake-bound, ringed by peaks, is the Engadin at its most contemplative.

items.name: Silvaplana, Windsurfing & Kitesurfing
items.description: The reliable afternoon 'Maloja wind' turns Lake Silvaplana into one of Europe's great high-altitude surfing arenas, from May to October the water fills with bright kites and sails against the Corvatsch backdrop. Even if you only watch from the shore over a lakeside lunch, it is one of the Engadin's most alive summer scenes; lessons and gear are on hand at the surf centre.

items.name: Zuoz, The Sgraffito Village
items.description: The best-preserved patrician village in the Upper Engadin, Zuoz is a picture-book ensemble of thick-walled Engadin houses with funnel windows, oriel bays and the incised, whitewashed wall-decoration called sgraffito. A guided village walk unlocks the stories behind the coats of arms and the fountains; unhurried, cultured, real.

items.name: S-chanf & the Upper Engadin Villages
items.description: Just beyond Zuoz, S-chanf marks the edge of the great flat river meadows and, with neighbouring Madulain and La Punt, offers the same sgraffito-fronted Engadin architecture without the crowds, plus the gateway to the Swiss National Park nearby. A quiet, authentic half-day for those who want the valley's soul, not its shop windows.

items.name: Pontresina, Belle Époque Village on the Bernina
items.description: A sunny, south-facing resort village of grand Belle Époque hotels and traditional sgraffito houses at the mouth of the Roseg and Morteratsch valleys, the walkers' and climbers' base of the Engadin, calmer than St. Moritz but with its own refined charm. The perfect launch point for the Bernina glaciers and valley hikes.

items.name: Celerina & the Chapel of San Gian
items.description: Celerina sits at the foot of Corviglia, where the Cresta Run and Olympia Bob Run finish, and is crowned by the landmark 15th-century chapel of San Gian with its twin (one roofless) towers on a low hill. A gentler, more village-scaled base than St. Moritz, minutes away by rail or road.

items.name: The Bernina Express
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes
items.description: The most spectacular Alpine rail journey runs from the Engadin over the Bernina Pass and down to palm-fringed Tirano in Italy, climbing past glaciers and looping through the celebrated Brusio spiral viaduct without a single rack rail. Ride it in the panoramic carriages, or splurge on the exclusive first-class 'Excellence Class' with dining service.

items.name: The Glacier Express
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes
items.description: Billed as the world's slowest express, the Glacier Express links St. Moritz to Zermatt over eight hours of viaducts, gorges and the Oberalp Pass, its Albula section part of the same UNESCO railway. The Excellence Class carriage, one seat per window, five-course lunch, a personal concierge, is the way HNI travellers do it.

items.name: The Landwasser Viaduct
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Rhaetian Railway in the Albula/Bernina Landscapes
items.description: The six-arched limestone viaduct that curves 65m above the Landwasser gorge straight into a tunnel mouth in the cliff is the single most photographed image of the Rhaetian Railway and the icon of the UNESCO line. Whether from a carriage window or the trackside viewpoint, it is the picture people come for.

items.name: The Val Roseg by Horse-Drawn Carriage
items.description: One of the most beautiful side valleys in the Engadin is reached the loveliest way, a horse-drawn carriage that clops from Pontresina station up the Rosegbach to the glacier-view Hotel Roseg, past larch woods and grazing meadows. Ride up, lunch on the terrace before the Bernina ice, and walk the gentle path back; a treat for all ages, and a sleigh ride in winter.

items.name: Val Fex, The Hidden Valley Above Sils
items.description: Car-free and impossibly pastoral, the Val Fex climbs behind Sils Maria to a scatter of hamlets, a frescoed mountain chapel and a small glacier at its head. Reached on foot or by horse-carriage (sleigh in winter), it is the Engadin's secret garden, a quiet, cultured escape favoured by those in the know.

items.name: The Engadin Lakes Hike
items.description: The classic valley-floor walk strings together the four Upper Engadin lakes, St. Moritz, Champfèr, Silvaplana and Sils, on easy, near-level paths, the water often mirror-still and the Bernina reflected in it. Flat enough for grandparents, beautiful enough for anyone; do it in sections and picnic at a shore of your choosing.

items.name: The Cresta Run
items.description: Built in 1884 and run by the storied St. Moritz Tobogganing Club, the Cresta is a 1.2km natural-ice skeleton track where riders hurl themselves head-first down a hand-built channel of snow and ice, one of only two natural-ice runs left in the world staging international competition. It used the same track for the skeleton event at both the 1928 and 1948 Winter Olympics; watching from Junction is a St. Moritz rite.

items.name: The Olympia Bob Run
items.description: The birthplace of bobsleigh, first raced here in 1904, is the last naturally built ice track in the world still hosting sanctioned bob and skeleton races, hand-carved each winter from snow and water alone. You can watch the professionals, or book a guest run and rocket down beside a pilot; St. Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics twice, in 1928 and 1948, and this track carried both.

items.name: Engadin Golf, The Oldest in Switzerland
items.description: Founded in Samedan in 1893, Engadin Golf is the oldest golf club in Switzerland and among the oldest in continental Europe, its flat valley-floor course ringed by 3,000m peaks and nicknamed the 'Swiss St. Andrews'. With a second course at Zuoz-Madulain and the high Kulm course above the village, it is high-altitude golf with an unmatched backdrop.

items.name: The Kempinski Alpine Spa & the Mauritius Spring
items.description: The Grand Hotel des Bains Kempinski stands on St. Moritz's 3,500-year-old bathing tradition, its vast Alpine Spa fed by the mineral-rich, naturally carbonated Mauritius spring that first made the town famous as a cure resort. Pools, Kneipp streams and thermal circuits make it one of the finest wellness addresses in the Alps.

items.name: The Palace Wellness at Badrutt's Palace
items.description: The spa of the legendary Badrutt's Palace, the address of St. Moritz society since 1896, offers ten treatment rooms, private spa suites, saunas and heated indoor-outdoor pools looking to the lake. Even non-residents can book treatments; it is discreet luxury at the beating heart of the resort.

items.name: The Kulm Spa & the Kulm Country Club
items.description: The Kulm Hotel, where Alpine winter tourism was famously invented on a bet in 1864, pairs a serene thermal-and-sauna wellness world with the Norman Foster-restored Kulm Country Club and the natural ice rink where the world's first Olympic ice events were held. History, wellness and glamour on one estate.

items.name: Via Serlas, The Luxury Mile
items.description: Reputed to be the world's shortest luxury shopping street, Via Serlas packs Chanel, Louis Vuitton, Gucci, Prada, Hermès, Cartier and Bulgari into a few glittering metres beside Badrutt's Palace. Around it, small St. Moritz institutions sell caviar, rare teas, Engadin specialities and fine watches, the whole resort's see-and-be-seen promenade.

items.name: Two Michelin Stars at IGNIV by Andreas Caminada
items.description: Andreas Caminada's playful fine-dining-as-sharing concept inside Badrutt's Palace holds two Michelin stars, beautifully composed modern European plates brought to the table to share, with the lake beyond the windows. One of the most sought-after tables in the Alps; reserve well ahead.

items.name: Da Vittorio, Two-Star Italian at the Carlton
items.description: The Cerea family's St. Moritz outpost of the famed Da Vittorio holds two Michelin stars for hearty-yet-refined Italian cooking, served in an elegant room above Lake St. Moritz, a natural favourite for guests who want gastronomy without ceremony overload, and staff attuned to dietary needs.

items.name: Ecco St. Moritz, Two Stars at Giardino Mountain
items.description: In the calm of Champfèr just outside the resort, Ecco within the Giardino Mountain hotel carries two Michelin stars for cuisine rooted in French tradition, the winter fine-dining destination for those who prefer their gastronomy a step removed from the St. Moritz throng.

items.name: Chesa Veglia, Badrutt's 17th-Century Farmhouse
items.description: A 1658 Engadin farmhouse turned into Badrutt's Palace's most atmospheric dining rooms, where pizza and grill are served under low painted beams and the après crowd gathers at the Polo Bar. Beautiful, historic and unmistakably St. Moritz, the enjoyable, less-formal counterpoint to the Michelin tables.

items.name: Mountain Biking the Engadin Trails
items.description: Beyond skiing, the Engadin is a serious summer bike destination, from easy, near-level lakeshore loops the whole family can ride to lift-served flow trails and technical high-alpine singletrack off Corviglia and Corvatsch. E-bikes and guides are easily arranged; a fine active day between the lakes and the peaks.

items.name: St. Moritz-Bad & Lake Staz (Lej da Staz)
items.description: A short walk or gentle carriage ride from the resort, the little forest-ringed Lej da Staz is the locals' summer swimming lake, warmer and calmer than the big lakes, with a rustic restaurant on its shore. A relaxed, unshowy escape that balances the glamour of the Dorf; lovely with children and grandparents.

items.name: Sailing & Rowing on Lake Silvaplana and Lake Sils
items.description: Two of the largest Alpine lakes in Graubünden, Silvaplana and Sils are prime high-altitude sailing water thanks to the dependable Maloja wind, and a graceful old passenger boat still crosses Lake Sils in summer. Charter a boat, take a sailing lesson, or simply cruise the mirror-calm mornings before the wind rises.

items.name: Alp Languard & the Marmot Trails Above Pontresina
items.description: A short chairlift from Pontresina lifts you to Alp Languard, a sunny alp famous for its bold, whistling marmots and easy family walks with the Bernina glaciers laid out opposite. Gentle, wildlife-rich and scenic, one of the Engadin's most rewarding low-effort mountain outings.

items.name: Heli-Skiing & Private Glacier Flights
items.description: For those who want the mountains to themselves, helicopters lift skiers to remote glacier descents and carry sightseers over the Bernina ice fields for a landing in the eternal snow. Arranged discreetly through the grand hotels or private guides, it is the Engadin at its most exclusive, and a spectacular multi-generational scenic flight in summer.

items.name: The Mili Weber House
items.description: The enchanting former home of illustrator Mili Weber, kept exactly as she left it and hand-painted with fairy-tale murals from floor to ceiling, a hidden, tender little gem quite unlike anything else in glamorous St. Moritz, visited by guided tour. A delightful, unexpected stop, especially with children.

items.name: Da Vittorio – St. Moritz
items.description: The Cerea family's Alpine outpost of their three-star Lombardy temple, widely held to be the finest Italian table in Switzerland.

items.name: Ecco St. Moritz
items.description: Reto Brändli's French-rooted cooking, depth and finesse in equal measure, in the calm of the Giardino Mountain.

items.name: IGNIV by Andreas Caminada
items.description: Caminada's fine-dining-meets-sharing concept inside Badrutt's Palace, generous, playful and technically exact.

items.name: Talvo by Dalsass
items.description: Mediterranean cooking of pure, produce-led essence in a 1658 Engadine farmhouse, one star, richly deserved.

items.name: The K by Tim Raue
items.description: Tim Raue's precise Asian-accented cooking, Berlin's two-star hand, brought to the Kulm's mountain room.

items.name: Cà d'Oro
items.description: Matthias Schmidberger's refined kitchen at the Kempinski, polished, contemporary and quietly excellent.

items.name: Grand Restaurant, Suvretta House
items.description: Fabrizio Zanetti's cooking in a coffered, candle-lit dining hall, old-world grandeur, thoroughly modern plates.

items.name: Matsuhisa by Nobu, St. Moritz
credentials: Part of the Nobu / Matsuhisa global group, at a MICHELIN Two-Key hotel
items.description: Nobu Matsuhisa's signature Japanese-Peruvian cooking, in the theatrical setting of Badrutt's Palace.

items.name: Dal Mulin
items.description: An independent village room of real ambition, Luca Porro's precise, personal cooking, free of any hotel.

items.name: Chesa Veglia
credentials: A genuine St. Moritz landmark, run by Badrutt's Palace (MICHELIN Two Keys, 2025)
items.description: A 1658 Engadine farmhouse owned by the Palace, pizza, grill and Alpine classics under carved timber and lantern light.

items.name: King's Social House
credentials: A Jason Atherton (multi-Michelin restaurateur) venue, inside Badrutt's Palace
items.description: Jason Atherton's restaurant-bar-club revival of Switzerland's oldest nightclub, a considered kitchen with a late tempo.

items.name: La Scarpetta
items.description: Honest, tasty Italian at a price the grand rooms can't touch, refined yet accessible, and new to the guide.

items.name: Renaissance Bar, Badrutt's Palace
credentials: Inside Badrutt's Palace, MICHELIN Two Keys (2025), The Leading Hotels of the World; a bar of genuine standing
items.description: The definitive St. Moritz hotel bar, timeless cocktails, a fireplace and a cigar selection, beneath the Palace's grandeur.

items.name: Dracula Club
credentials: A genuine St. Moritz institution, Gunter Sachs's private club (est. 1974), host of the Festival da Jazz
items.description: The legendary members' club founded by Gunter Sachs in the 1970s, 150 seats, and the private soul of St. Moritz nightlife.

items.name: King's Social House
credentials: A Jason Atherton venue inside Badrutt's Palace (MICHELIN Two Keys, 2025); the resort's storied club since the 1960s
items.description: Switzerland's oldest nightclub, reborn by Jason Atherton, dinner, drinks and roaming international DJs under the Palace.

plan.heading: 3 days in St. Moritz, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Coffee at the Hanselmann konditorei, then a walk along the frozen or blue lake below the Leaning Tower.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Segantini Museum for the Alpine painter, then the boutiques of the Via Serlas.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Ecco St. Moritz in the Giardino Mountain at Champfèr, two Michelin stars, then a drink at Badrutt's Palace.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Bernina railway toward the Morteratsch glacier, one of the great Alpine rail lines.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at El Paradiso above the lake, then a walk through the larch woods to Pontresina.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: The Grand Restaurant at Badrutt's Palace, or the intimate King's Club for a later, livelier night.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: Snow, sun, and the good life

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Corviglia by funicular for the runs or simply the terrace at La Marmite, the mountain restaurant above the town.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The thermal waters at the Kempinski or Kulm spa, unhurried.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A last dinner at IGNIV by Andreas Caminada in the Grand Hotel Kronenhof at Pontresina, the sharing table by candlelight.

items.name: St. Moritz Dorf
items.description: The upper village of grand hotels and boutiques, for those who want to be at the centre of it.

items.name: St. Moritz Bad
items.description: By the lake and spa springs, quieter and a shade more relaxed than Dorf.

items.name: Suvretta
items.description: A hushed, wooded pocket above town for people who want privacy and ski-in access.

events.name: Snow Polo World Cup St. Moritz
events.note: Three days of top-level polo on the frozen lake.

events.name: White Turf
events.note: Horse racing and skijoring across three Sundays on the lake.

events.name: St. Moritz Gourmet Festival
events.note: Visiting chefs cook across the town's hotels over a week.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: At around 1,800m the air is thin and dry, so ease in; St. Moritz is a see-and-be-seen resort in high season, so book the Badrutt's Palace or Kulm well ahead and time a visit around the winter polo or White Turf if that appeals.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Most arrive by private car or helicopter, or by the scenic Engadin rail line; the nearest airports are Zurich (about three hours by car) and Samedan for private jets, minutes away.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private car and driver handles the valley in winter snow; the village and lakeside are walkable, and hotel cars run guests to the slopes.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Reliable across the resort and valley; an eSIM activates on arrival and hotel wifi is strong.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Swiss francs (CHF); cards are universal and tipping stays modest, round up or leave a little for good service.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: December to March is the classic winter season with dependable snow and the frozen-lake events; July to September is bright and dry for hiking. April to May and November are quiet closure months best avoided.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Fly into Zurich (direct from Delhi on SWISS or Air India, ~8h45), then about 3.5-4 hours by rail via Chur, or arrive in style on the Glacier Express. No direct train, so the change at Chur is the norm; the final stretch is one of the finest alpine rail rides in Europe.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations needed; extremely safe and discreet. St. Moritz lies at ~1,800 m, high enough that some guests feel the thin air on day one, so pace yourself, hydrate, and go easy with alcohol at first. Tap water is excellent.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian food is well catered for in the grand hotels, which are used to international and Indian guests. For Jain specifics, give your hotel notice; standalone Indian restaurants are few, so plan meals through the property.
